newsitem.title: USA: Wis. committee hopes for budget vote Monday.
newsitem.headline: Wis. committee hopes for budget vote Monday.

text.p: Members of Wisconsin's Joint Finance Committee hope to vote Monday on a proposed $36 billion all-funds state budget for the fiscal biennium beginning July 1, a legislative aide said.

An announced $215 million settlement of a pension fund lawsuit Friday delayed the committee's scheduled completion of their budget review last week, said Robert Allen, an aide to Sen. Brian Burke who co-chairs the joint committee.
Lawmakers had been debating plans to account for a projected $230 million revenue surplus when they received word of the settlement in the 10-year-old trust fund case, Allen said.
Committee members sought to resolve the pension issue before resuming their review of the proposed budget on Monday afternoon, Allen said.
The committee does not anticipate increases in income or sales taxes in the budget, but may recommend increases in lesser taxes, Allen said.
The committee has recommended approval of a 1-cent-per gallon gasoline tax increase and raising annual motor vehicle registration fees from $40 to $45 per license plate, he said.
Recommendations from the joint finance committee are referred to the legislature for further consideration, Allen said. Lawmakers hope to complete the budget by the end of June, he said.
